s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with evidence of cardiac dysfunction and conduction abnormalities
salient_findings: New left bundle branch block on ECG
Moderate-size area of inferior wall ischaemia and scar on pharmacological nuclear stress test
Intermittent high-grade AV block with ventricular escape beats on telemetry
key_facts: 50-year-old man with a remote history of treated Lyme disease
No hypertension, hyperlipidemia, or diabetes
Four episodes of syncope over 24 hours
Initial workup six weeks earlier was unrevealing
New left bundle branch block on outpatient ECG
Exercise stress testing provoked presyncope with a brief burst of atrial tachycardia
LVEF of 42% with a moderate-size area of inferior wall ischaemia and scar on pharmacological nuclear stress test
No chest pain or heart failure symptoms
Vital signs: blood pressure 140/66 mmHg, heart rate 54 bpm, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, temperature 36.2°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air
Physical examination was unremarkable
12-lead ECG showed sinus rhythm at 57 bpm, first-degree AV block, and a prolonged QTc
Brief burst of atrial tachycardia that resolved with IV metoprolol
Cardiac enzymes, thyroid function tests, serum calcium, and ACE levels were normal
Lyme antibody testing was negative
Chest radiograph was normal
Transthoracic echocardiography showed an LVEF of 45–50% with no regional wall motion abnormalities
Telemetry captured intermittent high-grade AV block with ventricular escape beats
Coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries
Left ventriculography showed an LVEF of 35–40%
Permanent dual-chamber pacemaker was implanted
Outpatient cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an LVEF of 31%, RV ejection fraction of 23%, and mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement in the basal anteroseptal wall
Contrast-enhanced CT scan of the chest showed mediastinal and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on CT scan, and cardiac dysfunction with conduction abnormalities

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Evidence of cardiac dysfunction, conduction abnormalities, and reduced RV ejection fraction

shortlist.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Reduced LVEF, evidence of cardiac dysfunction, and conduction abnormalities

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Prolonged QTc interval on ECG and history of syncope

shortlist.label: Cardiac amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Not explicitly listed, but possible given the combination of cardiac dysfunction, conduction abnormalities, and lymphadenopathy

raw.rationale: The combination of reduced LVEF, high-grade AV block, and mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI, along with mediastinal and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on CT scan, are highly suggestive of cardiac sarcoidosis.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's cardiac MRI showed mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement in the basal anteroseptal wall, which is not typical for arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a reduced LVEF, the presence of lymphadenopathy and specific cardiac MRI findings suggest a more specific diagnosis than dilated cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: Although the patient has a prolonged QTc, the other findings such as reduced LVEF, high-grade AV block, and lymphadenopathy are not typical for long QT syndrome.

rejected.label: Cardiac amyloidosis
rejected.why: The patient's cardiac MRI did not show the typical amyloidosis pattern of subendocardial or transmural late gadolinium enhancement, and the presence of lymphadenopathy is not typical for cardiac amyloidosis.
